title: CHAPTER 2 : THEORY OF DEMAND AND DETERMINANTS
content:
👋 ሰላም! ውድ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች! Chapter 1ን በስኬት አጠናቀን ዛሬ ደግሞ ወደ እጅግ ወሳኙ እና ማራኪው Chapter 2 (Theory of Demand and Supply) በደስታ ገብተናል! 🚀

በዚህ የመጀመሪያ ክፍል የ Demand ትርጉም፣ Law of Demand፣ Demand Schedule፣ Demand Curve፣ Demand Function (ከነ ስሌቱ)፣ Individual vs Market Demand እንዲሁም Determinants of Demand (Demand Shifters) እና Movement along vs Shift in Demand Curveን በዝርዝር እንመለከታለን። እስከ መጨረሻው አብራችሁን ሁኑ! 👇👇👇


2.1 Theory of Demand

Brainstorming Questions:
1. Are demand and want similar? Why?
2. Why can't we purchase all that we need or we desire to have?
3. Can we say that, with a decrease in the price of a commodity, a consumer normally buys more of it? Why?
4. Explain why demand curves always slope downwards from left to right. Are there any exceptions to this?

Demand is one of the forces determining prices. The theory of demand is related to the economic activities of consumers-consumption. Hence, the purpose of the theory of demand is to determine the various factors that affect demand.

In our day-to-day life, we use the word 'demand' in a loose sense to mean a desire of a person to purchase a commodity or service. But in economics, it has a specific meaning, which is different from what we use it in our day-to-day activities.

Demand implies more than a mere desire to purchase a commodity. It states that the consumer must be willing and able to purchase the commodity which he/she desires. His/her desire should be backed by his/her purchasing power.

• A poor person is willing to buy a car; it has no significance, since he/she has no ability to pay for it.
• On the other hand, if his/her desire to buy the car is backed by the purchasing power, then this constitutes demand.

Demand, thus, means the desire of the consumer for a commodity backed by purchasing power. These two factors are essential:
1. If a consumer is willing to buy but is not able to pay, his/her desire will not become demand.
2. Similarly, if the consumer has the ability to pay but is not willing to pay, his/her desire will not be called demand.

More specifically, demand refers to various quantities of a commodity or service that a consumer would purchase at a given time in a market at various prices, given other things unchanged (ceteris paribus). The quantity demanded of a particular commodity depends on the price of that commodity.

Law of Demand:
This is the principle of demand, which states that, price of a commodity and its quantity demanded are inversely related i.e., as price of a commodity increases (decreases), quantity demanded for that commodity decreases (increases), ceteris paribus.

👉 የፍላጎት ፅንሰ-ሀሳብ (Theory of Demand) :
በዕለት ተዕለት ህይወታችን 'Demand' እና 'Want/Desire' (መመኘት) አንድ ይመስሉናል፤ በኢኮኖሚክስ ግን በፍፁም ልዩነት አላቸው! 😅
• Desire (ምኞት) ብቻ፦ ለምሳሌ አንድ ተማሪ አዲስ iPhone የመግዛት ፍላጎት ቢኖረው ነገር ግን የሚከፍለው ገንዘብ (Purchasing power) ከሌለው ይሄ ምኞት እንጂ Demand አይባልም።
• Effective Demand (እውነተኛ ፍላጎት)፦ ፍላጎት (Willingness) + የመክፈል አቅም (Ability to pay) ሲኖሩ ብቻ ነው ፍላጎታችን በኢኮኖሚክስ ቋንቋ Demand የሚባለው።
• Law of Demand (የፍላጎት ህግ)፦ የዕቃ ዋጋ (Price) እና የሚፈለገው መጠን (Quantity Demanded) የተቃራኒ/የግልባጭ (Inverse) ግንኙነት አላቸው። ዋጋ ሲጨምር የምንገዛው መጠን ይቀንሳል፤ ዋጋ ሲቀንስ ደግሞ የምንገዛው መጠን ይጨምራል (Ceteris Paribus - ሌሎች ነገሮች ባሉበት ሳይቀየሩ ቢቀጥሉ)።

💡 Exam Hint: Willingness vs Ability
በፈተና ላይ "Demand = Willingness + Ability to pay" መሆኑን እንዳትረሱ! አንዱ ከሌለ Demand ሊባል አይችልም። በተጨማሪም Ceteris Paribus ማለት "All other things remaining constant" ማለት ነው።


2.1.1 Demand Schedule (Table), Demand Curve, and Demand Function

The relationship that exists between price and the amount of a commodity purchased can be represented by a table (schedule), a curve, or an equation.

1. Demand Schedule:
Demand schedule can be constructed for any commodity if the list of prices and quantities purchased at those prices are known. An individual demand schedule is a list of the various quantities of a commodity, which an individual consumer purchases at various levels of prices in the market. A demand schedule states the relationship between price and quantity demanded in a table form.

Table 2.1: Individual household demand for orange per week

Price per kg (Birr)54321
Quantity demanded/week5791113

2. Demand Curve:
Demand curve is a graphical representation of the relationship between different quantities of a commodity demanded by an individual at different prices per time period.

Figure 2.1: Individual demand curve

In the above diagram prices of oranges are given on 'OY' axis and quantity demanded on 'OX' axis. For example, when the price per kilogram is birr 1 the quantity demanded is 13 kilograms. From the above figure you may notice that as the price declines quantity demanded increases and vice-versa.

3. Demand Function:
Demand function is a mathematical relationship between price and quantity demanded, all other things remaining the same. A typical demand function is given by:

Q_d = f(P)

where Q_d is quantity demanded and P is price of the commodity, in our case price of orange.

Example: Let the demand function be Q = a + bP

b = ΔQ / ΔP (e.g. moving from point A to B on figure 2.1 above)

b = (7 - 5) / (4 - 5) = -2, where b is the slope of the demand curve

Q = a - 2P, to find a, substitute price either at point A or B.

7 = a - 2(4) ⇒ a = 15

Therefore, Q = 15 - 2P is the demand function for orange in the above numerical example.

👉 Demand Schedule, Curve እና Function :
• Demand Schedule (ሰንጠረዥ)፦ በዋጋ እና በፍላጎት መጠን መካከል ያለውን ግንኙነት በሰንጠረዥ ያሳያል።
• Demand Curve (ግራፍ)፦ ይሄው ሰንጠረዥ በግራፍ ሲሳል ከግራ ወደ ቀኝ ወደ ታች የሚወርድ (Downward Sloping) ግራፍ ይሰጠናል። ይሄም የሚያሳየው የ Inverse Relationshipን ህግ ነው!
• Demand Function (ቀመር)፦ በሒሳባዊ መንገድ Q_d = a + bP ብለን እንገልጸዋለን።
  - a = Intercept (ዋጋ 0 ሲሆን የሚኖረው የፍላጎት መጠን)
  - b = Slope (የግራፉ ተዳፋት ሲሆን ሁሌም Negative/አሉታዊ ነው፣ ምክንያቱም የ Inverse ህግን ስለሚከተል!)


Individual and Market Demand

Market Demand: The market demand schedule, curve or function is derived by horizontally adding the quantity demanded for the product by all buyers at each price.

The following graph depicts market demand curve at price equal to 3:

Figure 2.2: Individual and Market demand curve

Numerical Example:
Suppose the individual demand function of a product is given by:
P = 10 - Q/2
and there are about 100 identical buyers in the market. Then the market demand function is given by:

First, express quantity Q in terms of price P:
P = 10 - Q/2 ⇔ Q/2 = 10 - P ⇔ Q = 20 - 2P

Now, multiply by the total number of buyers (N = 100):
Q_m = (20 - 2P) × 100 = 2000 - 200P

👉 የገበያ ፍላጎት (Market Demand) :
የገበያ ፍላጎት ማለት በገበያው ውስጥ ያሉ ሁሉንም ተጠቃሚዎች /ገዢዎች ፍላጎት በአግድም በመደመር (Horizontal Summation) የሚገኝ ውጤት ነው!
• ለምሳሌ በ 3 ብር ዋጋ፦ Consumer 1 (5 እቃ) + Consumer 2 (7 እቃ) + Consumer 3 (2 እቃ) = Market Demand (14 እቃ) ይሆናል።
• በስሌት ጊዜ፦ መጀመሪያ የግለሰቡን ቀመር ወደ Q = ... መለወጥ፣ ከዚያም አጠቃላይ ገዢዎች ብዛት (N) ማባዛት እንዳትረሱ! 😉

💡 Exam Hint: Horizontal Summation Trick
ፈተና ላይ P = 10 - Q/2 ተሰጥቶ አጠቃላይ የገበያ ቀመር ፈልጉ ከተባላችሁ ቀጥታ በ 100 እንዳታበዙት! መጀመሪያ Q ን ሰብጀክት አድርጉ (Q = 20 - 2P)፣ ከዚያ በኋላ ነው በ 100 የምታበዙት!


2.1.2 Determinants of Demand

The demand for a product is influenced by many factors. Some of these factors are:
I. Price of the product
II. Taste or preference of consumers
III. Income of the consumers
IV. Price of related goods
V. Consumers expectation of income and price
VI. Number of buyers in the market

When we state the law of demand, we kept all the factors to remain constant except the price of the good. A change in any of the above listed factors except the price of the good will change the demand, while a change in the price, other factors remain constant will bring change in quantity demanded.

• Change in Demand: A change in demand will shift the demand curve from its original location. For this reason, those factors listed above other than price are called demand shifters.
• Change in Quantity Demanded: A change in own price is only a movement along the same demand curve.

Changes in Demand (Shifts in Demand Curve):
A change in any determinant of demand—except the good's price—causes the demand curve to shift. We call this a change in demand. If buyers choose to purchase more at any price, the demand curve shifts rightward—an increase in demand. If buyers choose to purchase less at any price, the demand curve shifts leftward—a decrease in demand.

Figure 2.3: Shift in demand curve

When demand increases, demand curve shifts upward/rightward (D₁) while a decrease in demand shifts demand curve downward/leftward (D₂).

Now let us examine how each factor affects demand:

I. Taste or Preference:
When the taste of a consumer changes in favour of a good, her/his demand will increase and the opposite is true.

II. Income of the Consumer:
Goods are classified into two categories depending on how a change in income affects their demand. These are normal goods and inferior goods.
• Normal Goods: Goods whose demand increases as income increases (Direct relationship).
• Inferior Goods: Goods whose demand is inversely related with income. In general, inferior goods are poor quality goods with relatively lower price, and buyers of such goods are expected to shift to better quality goods as their income increases.
Note: The classification of goods into normal and inferior is subjective and dependent on socio-economic development.

III. Price of Related Goods:
Two goods are said to be related if a change in the price of one good affects the demand for another good. There are two types of related goods:
• Substitute Goods: Goods which satisfy the same desire of the consumer (e.g., Tea and Coffee, Pepsi and Coca-Cola). If two goods are substitutes, price of one and demand for the other are directly related (If Price of Coffee ↑ ⇒ Demand for Tea ↑).
• Complementary Goods: Goods which are jointly consumed (e.g., Car and Fuel, Tea and Sugar). If two goods are complements, price of one and demand for the other are inversely related (If Price of Fuel ↑ ⇒ Demand for Car ↓).

IV. Consumer Expectation of Income and Price:
Higher future price expectation will increase current demand, while a lower future price expectation will decrease current demand.

V. Number of Buyers in the Market:
Since market demand is the horizontal sum of individual demand, an increase in the number of buyers will increase demand while a decrease in the number of buyers will decrease demand.

👉 ፍላጎትን የሚወስኑ ነገሮች (Determinants of Demand) :
ይህ በፈተና ላይ በጣም የሚደጋገም ወሳኝ ነጥብ ነው! በጥንቃቄ እንያዘው፦

• Movement along the Curve vs. Shift in Curve:
  1. የእቃው የራሱ ዋጋ (Own Price) ከተቀየረ፦ በቋሚው የ Demand Curve ላይ እንቅስቃሴ ብቻ ያደርጋል (Movement along the curve ይባላል)። ይሄም Change in Quantity Demanded ይባላል።
  2. ከዋጋ ውጪ ያሉ ሌሎች ነገሮች (Shifters) ከተቀየሩ፦ ሙሉው Graph ወደ ቀኝ ወይም ወደ ግራ ይንቀሳቀሳል (Shift ያደርጋል)። ይሄም Change in Demand ይባላል።

• የ Shifters ዝርዝር፦
  • Income (ገቢ)፦ ለ Normal Goods ገቢ ሲጨምር ፍላጎት ይጨምራል፤ ለ Inferior Goods (ዝቅተኛ ጥራት ያላቸው) ደግሞ ገቢ ሲጨምር ፍላጎታቸው ይቀንሳል (ምክንያቱም ሰዎች የተሻለ ጥራት ወደለው ይሸጋገራሉ)።
  • Substitutes (ተኪ እቃዎች - ለምሳሌ ሻይና ቡና)፦ የቡና ዋጋ ቢወደድ ሰዎች ቡና መጣጣታቸውን ትተው ሻይ መጠጣት ስለሚጀምሩ የሻይ ፍላጎት ይጨምራል (Direct Relationship)።
  • Complements (አጋዥ እቃዎች - ለምሳሌ መኪናና ቤንዚን)፦ የቤንዚን ዋጋ ጣሪያ ቢነካ የመኪና ፍላጎት ይቀንሳል (Inverse Relationship)።
  • Future Expectation (የወደፊት ግምት)፦ ነገ የዘይት ዋጋ ይወደዳል ተብሎ ከተገመተ፣ ዛሬ ሰዎች በብዛት ስለሚገዙ የዛሬው ፍላጎት ይጨምራል!

💡 Summary Box for Exam Success:
• Own Price Change ⇒ Movement along the curve (Change in Quantity Demanded)
• Non-price Determinants Change ⇒ Shift of the curve (Change in Demand)
• Substitute Goods Price ↑ ⇒ Demand for target good ↑
• Complementary Goods Price ↑ ⇒ Demand for target good ↓
